sources.title: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill beats forecasts as it battles Lilly
Continental raises 2026 outlook on tyre business strength
Oracle abandons $7 billion Tencent AI deal under Trump pressure, FT reports
Meta raises $15 billion in five-part US bond sale to fund AI expansion

stories.headline: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy-pill sales beat estimates; 2026 guidance raised
stories.body: Wegovy pill third-quarter revenue DKK5.39bn, versus company-compiled consensus DKK4.62bn, up 53% from Q2. Adjusted operating profit DKK31.72bn vs DKK28.39bn expected; adjusted sales DKK79.20bn vs DKK73.22bn expected. Adjusted 2026 sales and operating-profit outlook at constant exchange rates raised to -2% through +2% from previous -6% through 0%.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Positive oral-obesity-drug adoption and better operating profits; monitor competitive pricing, Lilly market share and sustainability of guidance.
stories.watch_next: Wegovy pill market share, 2026 profit delivery and forthcoming Lilly results.

stories.headline: Continental raises 2026 operating-margin outlook on tyre strength
stories.body: Continental raised FY2026 operating profit margin guidance excluding discontinued ContiTech to 13.4%-14%. Previous range was 12%-13.5%; company-supplied analyst consensus stood at 13.7%.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Better tyre margins modestly improve earnings expectations; does not imply a broad recovery in European manufacturing.
stories.watch_next: Actual reported margins, tyre demand, restructuring and credit metrics.

stories.headline: Reuters relays unconfirmed FT report of Oracle–Tencent US$7bn AI deal cancellation
stories.body: Reuters relayed a Financial Times report alleging cancellation of an estimated US$7 billion Oracle–Tencent AI-chip lease involving about 100,000 chips at Southeast Asian data centres. Reuters could not independently verify the claim; company confirmation was unavailable.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: If confirmed, trade controls could alter cloud revenue assumptions, asset utilisation and China/SEA data-centre buildout financing. Cancellation is not confirmed by Oracle or Reuters independently.
stories.watch_next: Official Oracle/Tencent statements, contractual status, cancellation costs and further US export-policy clarifications.

stories.headline: Meta US$15bn bond offering: 2031 and 2033 tranche coupons reviewed
stories.body: The Reuters account gives US$3.25 billion of Meta notes due in 2031 carrying a 5.85% coupon and US$3.25 billion due in 2033 at a 6.25% coupon, with Moody's assigning Aa3. The time these terms first appeared is unknown. Coupon does not establish issue yield.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Coupon and issue yield are not interchangeable; credit evaluation requires final issue price, maturity-specific UST spreads, leverage and expected capex.
stories.watch_next: Full tranche pricing, issue yields, benchmark spreads and free-cash-flow/debt trajectory.
